A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same L2D research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite additions and renumbering in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original Llama and Qwen experiments on mathematics, coding, and knowledge tasks, with ablations and additional evaluations in Appendices C–D.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds original search, best-of-N, evaluation-sensitivity, reasoning-model, and chain-of-thought comparisons.

M1.justification: The core architecture, diffusion objective, conditioning, and training procedure remain unchanged. Section 4.3 adds an evaluated inference extension combining L2D with beam search, allocating half the original budget to each component. This extends decoding without redesigning L2D.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same curated SmolTalk training coverage and nine evaluation benchmarks, including the appendix tasks. V2's additional models, prompting variants, answer extraction, and pass@K evaluations change procedures within these retained tasks rather than adding datasets or domains.

E2.justification: V1 primarily compares against untuned models, LoRA, and full finetuning. V2 adds evaluated token-search and chain-of-thought comparators and DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B, together with combinations involving L2D (Tables 2 and 16–18). This substantially broadens comparison with alternative inference-scaling approaches.

E3.justification: The original training settings and main evaluation remain. New protocols include 15-hypothesis beam search, pass@5/10 evaluation for mathematics and knowledge, and a separate GSM8K setup using eight examples, greedy baseline decoding, and relaxed extraction. Appendix D.7 also introduces modified reasoning-model prompts and parsing, plus longer chain-of-thought demonstrations. These are additional settings, not evidence that the original experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The existing learning-rate, noise-scale, initialization, velocity, and solver analyses are retained. V2 adds substantial analyses of oracle best-of-N scaling, sensitivity to GSM8K evaluation choices, and complementarity with search, chain-of-thought prompting, and an R1-distilled model. These test additional questions about when L2D helps and how its benefits combine with other approaches.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-training uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional pass@K evaluations concern sampling budgets and success metrics, not uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Matched original results are retained, including Table 1 and the existing appendix ablations. Substantial new results appear in Tables 13 and 15–17 and the search rows of Tables 2 and 18: token search scores 33.83 overall and its L2D combination 38.57. The new relaxed GSM8K evaluation gives Llama 1B full finetuning 46.36 versus L2D 43.41; the original setup's 33.48 versus 38.86 remains unchanged. These are additional conditions, not same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), the single-step diffusion interpretation, and the midpoint integration derivation are retained. V2 adds no substantive formal assumptions, theoretical results, or proofs; its beam-search scoring description supplies implementation information.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains diffusion finetuning that preserves the original model while enabling additional inference computation. The abstract and introduction qualify superiority from 'is more effective' to 'can be more effective' and extend the claimed complementarity from traditional finetuning to search. These refine the scope without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Section 6 and Appendix D.6 newly acknowledge limitations in accessing confidence scores and directly controlling sampling through logits. V2 explains that relaxed GSM8K evaluation changes comparative advantages, that oracle verification can favor repeated sampling, and that R1-style reasoning introduces substantial costs and task tradeoffs. These materially qualify applicability and strengthen the interpretation of complementarity.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the promised code release with a repository link and a statement that code is provided, while removing Appendix B.1's separate data-release promise. It adds beam-search scoring and sampling details, clarifies the main evaluation's untempered generation, and describes new prompt-generation and parsing procedures. The existing hyperparameter table and dataset preparation recipe remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 substantially broadens positioning relative to search, repeated sampling, and contemporary reasoning approaches, adding discussion and citations for DeepSeek-R1, s1, inference-compute scaling, and diffusion alignment. Sections 6 and D.4–D.7 explicitly position L2D as complementary to these approaches. The earlier diffusion-model relationships remain, while the Lightman and Ye references are removed.

P1.justification: V2 makes targeted wording corrections, clarifies method explanations, and revises the related-work and discussion prose. It inserts search and expanded appendix subsections, acknowledgements, and an impact statement. The main six-section organization and Appendices A–D remain recognizable; the revision is chiefly added scientific content rather than extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: V2 adds four substantive comparison tables for best-of-N, relaxed GSM8K, R1-style reasoning, and chain-of-thought, and expands the extension tables with search rows. Existing plots retain their content but are resized or relocated, and Figure 5's reversed math/coding caption is corrected. The new Table 13 introduces a labeling error by placing MMLU columns under 'Coding'.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the central test-time-scaling argument by adding direct comparisons with alternative scaling approaches, which v1 largely lacked. More importantly, Table 15 exposes evaluation-dependent rankings, while Section 6 and Appendix D.6 explain consequential sampling and confidence limitations. This improves the credibility and calibration of the conclusions. Differing comparison settings and the continued absence of uncertainty estimates still limit some conclusions, but do not outweigh these gains.
